subject: installing plry in R 2.7.1 on Debian Lenny

messages.author: d5c26533dc44f3c0
messages.subject: installing plry in R 2.7.1 on Debian Lenny
parts:
I've not used R a whole lot on Linux but I have recently been working
on getting some of my code ported to Amazon Elastic MapReduce which
runs a slightly doctored version of Debian Lenny and the "r-
recommended" set up which is R 2.7.1. Link to more info on r-
recommended at the bottom.Some of the discussion lists for AMZN
elastic M/R make it sound like one cannot install R packages inside
the nodes. I've proven to myself that this is false by successfully
downloading and installing Hmisc on the nodes. I installed Hmisc like
this:

options(repos=c(CRAN="http://streaming.stat.iastate.edu/CRAN/"))
dir.create("~/R/")
install.packages("Hmisc", lib="~/R/")
require(Hmisc, lib="~/R/")

When I try the same approach with plyr I get an error that "plyr"
cannot be found following the install.packages("plyr", lib="~/R/")
step.

Any tips on why this install method does not work? R 2.7.1 seems to
load plyr fine in Windows. Thanks for any and all suggestions on how I
might debug this.

-JD Long

http://packages.debian.org/lenny/r-recommended

hadley, thanks to your recommendation via twitter to try editing the
DESCRIPTION file and lower the dependency to 2.7 I was able to get
plyr installed on 2.7.1 in Debian. I then had to add the addNA()
function to my code. I didn't realize that R was parsing the
description file to get required version.

-JD Long
